n: In that day the Lord will slay Leviathan, the twisting sea serpent and dragon. In ancient stories this monster stood for chaos; here it symbolizes evil powers and, ultimately, Satan.

f.g: A legendary sea monster representing chaos and evil (Job 41; Psalms 74:14).

n: In that day sing about a delightful vineyard! This new song reverses Isaiah’s sad vineyard song in chapter 5.
The Lord Himself tends this vineyard, watering it constantly and guarding it day and night so nothing harms it.

f.w: I the LORD do keep it

n: God is not angry with His vineyard now. If briers and thorns (enemies) attacked, He would march against them and burn them up.
Better yet, let enemies take hold of God’s protection and make peace with Him. The repetition shows God’s eager invitation.

f.g: Grasp my refuge — seek safety in me.

n: In days to come Jacob will take root, Israel will blossom and bud, and fill the whole world with fruit. Latter-day Saints see Israel’s gathering and missionary work as part of this fulfillment.

f.w: fill the face of the world with fruit

n: Has God struck Israel as hard as He struck Israel’s attackers? No — His discipline of His people is measured and merciful.
God dealt with Israel in measured ways, sending them into exile, removing them with His fierce wind as on a day of the hot east wind — but holding back His harshest blast.

f.g: With moderation; possibly “by driving her away.”

n: This is how Jacob’s sin will be removed: when Israel smashes its pagan altars like crushed chalk, and no Asherah poles or incense altars remain standing.
The fortified city of the proud will be desolate and empty like a wilderness, where calves graze and strip the branches.
When its branches dry up, women will break them off for firewood. These are people without understanding, so their Maker will not show them favor.
In that day the Lord will thresh His harvest from the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt, and gather His people one by one. Each person matters to Him.

f.g: The Wadi of Egypt, Israel’s southwestern border.

n: A great trumpet will sound, and those lost in Assyria and outcasts in Egypt will come and worship the Lord on the holy mountain at Jerusalem — a picture of the great latter-day gathering.

f.w: the great trumpet shall be blown
